rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabrisi rejects abrogating the certain Qur'anic rule with a report that, even if sound, establishes only probability.
rows.anchor: فقد أبعد لأن الخبر لو سلم من كل قدح لكان يقتضي الظن ولا يجوز أن ينسخ كتاب الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the no-bequest-for-an-heir report is accepted despite criticism of its transmitter, it can specify the verse: an heir may receive a bequest up to one third, not beyond it.
rows.anchor: لخصصنا عموم الآية وحملناها على أنه لا وصية لوارث بما يزيد على الثلث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Consensus that a bequest is not obligatory does not prove abrogation, since a recommended and encouraged act need not be obligatory.
rows.anchor: الإجماع إنما هو على أنها لا تفيد الفرض وذلك لا يمنع من كونها مندوبا إليها مرغبا فيها

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Asked whether a bequest to an heir is permissible, Abu Jaʿfar answered yes and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام أنه سئل هل تجوز الوصية للوارث فقال: نعم وتلا هذه الآية

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī says that dying without a bequest for close relatives who do not inherit ends one's deeds in disobedience.
rows.anchor: السكوني عن أبي عبد الله عن أبيه عن علي ع قال: من لم يوص عند موته لذوي قرابته

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says that one who dies without a will dies a death of the pre-Islamic age.
rows.anchor:
النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:
" من مات بغير وصية مات ميتة جاهلية "

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to call a person's failure to make a sound will before death a deficiency in character and intellect.
rows.anchor:
النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:
" من مات بغير وصية مات ميتة جاهلية "
وعنه عليه السلام أنه قال:

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu ʿAbd Allāh says a Muslim should not go to sleep without keeping his will beneath his head.
rows.anchor:
أبي عبد الله عليه السلام أنه قال:
" ما ينبغي لامرىء مسلم أن يبيت إلا ووصيته تحت رأسه "

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that breaking the fast while traveling is a firm obligation, not merely a concession.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال: الإفطار في إلسفر عزيمة.

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh compares fasting during Ramadan travel to breaking the fast while at home.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله أنه قال: الصائم في شهر رمضان في السفر كالمفطر فيه في الحضور

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh says he would not perform the funeral prayer for a man who died fasting during a journey.
rows.anchor: وعنه ع قال: لو أن رجلا مات صائما في السفر لما صليت عليه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says a traveler breaks the fast and shortens prayer, except when traveling to hunt or to commit disobedience to God.
rows.anchor: صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " من سافر أفطر وقصر إلا أن يكون رجلا سفره إلى صيد

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī transmits from Muḥammad ibn Muslim that the Prophet first broke a Ramadan journey fast at Kurāʿ al-Ghamīm, ordered the people to break theirs, and called those who continued disobedient; the name persisted until his death.
rows.anchor: إلى محمد بن مسلم عن أبي عبد الله قال: لم يكن رسول الله يصوم في السفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most scholars take the pronoun in this phrase to refer to fasting: those able to fast initially could either fast without expiation or break the fast and feed a poor person per day.
rows.anchor: الهاء: يعود إلى الصوم عند أكثر أهل العلم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Abū Muslim instead take the pronoun to refer to the ransom or feeding payment.
rows.anchor: الهاء يعود إلى الفداء عن الحسن وأبي مسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Shaʿbī understand the phrase to cover all people under an initial choice between fasting and feeding, later abrogated by the command to fast when present for Ramadan.
rows.anchor: أنه ساير الناس كما قدمنا ذكره من التخيير والنسخ بعده وهو قول ابن عباس والشعبي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and ʿAṭāʾ say the original concession covered pregnant and nursing women and the very old; the pregnant and nursing were later excluded, while the elderly person's concession remained.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الرخصة كانت للحوامل والمراضع والشيخ الفاني ثم نسخ من الآية الحامل والمرضع وبقي الشيخ الكبير

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says this concerns people who formerly could fast but became unable, so there is no abrogation.
rows.anchor: أن معناه وعلى الذين كانوا يطيقونه ثم صاروا بحيث لا يطيقونه ولا نسخ فيه عن السدي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from Abū ʿAbd Allāh says that an older person or someone afflicted by thirst after previously being able to fast owes one mudd of food daily.
rows.anchor: رواه بعض أصحابنا عن أبي عبد الله أن معناه وعلى الذين كانوا يطيقون الصوم ثم أصابهم كبر أو عطاش

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Through ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, al-Ṣādiq says a person who missed Ramadan through illness, recovered, but did not make it up before the next Ramadan owes both make-up fasting and one mudd of food per missed day.
rows.anchor: بإسناده عن الصادق ع وعلى الذين يطيقونه فدية من مرض في شهر رمضان فأفطر ثم صح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iraqis set the fidya at half a ṣāʿ per day, al-Shāfiʿī at one mudd, and the Imāmī position at two mudd for the able person or one mudd if unable.
rows.anchor: اختلف في مقدار الفدية فقال أهل العراق: نصف صاع عن كل يوم وقال الشافعي: عن كل يوم مد

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and Ṭāwūs interpret voluntary extra good as feeding more than one poor person.
rows.anchor: معناه من أطعم أكثر من مسكين واحد عن عطاء وطاوس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets it as giving one poor person more than the adequate amount, beyond half a ṣāʿ.
rows.anchor: أطعم المسكين الواحد أكثر من قدر الكفاية حتى يزيده على نصف صاع عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reconciles the preceding views: voluntary good means increasing the amount of food given.
rows.anchor: قول ابن عباس: من تطوع بزيادة الإطعام

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan gives another reading: the phrase means doing good in combining religious practices.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه من عمل برا في جمع الدين فهو خير له عن الحسن

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī understands the phrase as fasting in addition to paying the fidya.
rows.anchor: وقيل من صام مع الفدية عن الزهري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison that fasting is better than fidya applied while paying fidya was permitted; after abrogation, breaking the fast is not lawful for those required to fast.
rows.anchor: وكان هذا مع جواز الفدية فأما بعد النسخ فلا يجوز أن يقال الصوم خير من الفدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says fasting is better for someone able to fast, and earns a greater reward than expiation for one unable to fast.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه الصوم خير لمطيقه وأفضل ثوابا من التكفير لمن أفطر بالعجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing condition is also read as meaning: if you know which deeds are best.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن كنتم تعلمون أفضل أعمالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabrisi takes the wording to indicate that capacity exists before the act is performed.
rows.anchor: دلالة على أن الاستطاعة قبل الفعل

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim reads ولتكملوا with a doubled consonant; the other readers use the lighter form.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم ولتكملوا بالتشديد والباقون لتكملوا بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads العسر and اليسر with the heavier articulation; the remaining readers use the lighter articulation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر العسر واليسر بالتثقيل فيهما والباقون بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading ولتكملوا is supported by the Qur'anic wording اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم.
rows.anchor:
ولتكملوا قوله:
اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: The other form is supported by the interchangeability of the فعل and أفعل patterns; al-Nābigha's verse uses كملت in this sense.
rows.anchor:
النابغة.
فكملت مائة منها حمامتها وأسرعت حسبة في ذلك العدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahr is the familiar word for month, pluralized as أشهر for a small number and شهور for larger numbers; its root concerns appearing, as the crescent makes a month known.
rows.anchor: الشهر معروف وجمعه في القلة أشهر وفي الكثرة شهور وأصله من اشتهاره بالهلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root شهَر also means to make something manifest or draw it out; a broad, heavy she-camel is also called شهيرة.
rows.anchor: شهرت الحديث: أظهرته وشهرت السيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramadan derives from intense heat striking sand; the months were named for their seasons, and Ramadan coincided with hot weather. Its plural includes رمضانات.
rows.anchor: وأصل رمضان من الرمض، وهو شدة وقع الشمس على الرمل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid reports that Ramadan is one of God's names and advises saying شهر رمضان because one cannot know what Ramadan is.
rows.anchor:
عن مجاهد:
" لا تقل رمضان ولكن قل شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report promises forgiveness of prior sins to whoever fasts Ramadan with faith and expectation of reward.
rows.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:
" من صام رمضان إيمانا واحتسابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed etymology says Ramadan was named because it burns away sins.
rows.anchor: سمي رمضان لأنه يرمض الذنوب أي يحرقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'an is connected to gathering: Arabs said a she-camel had not gathered her womb around a foetus, and reading gathers letters together.
rows.anchor: والقرآن أصله الجمع لقولهم ما قرأت الناقة سلأ قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Furqān means that which distinguishes truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: والفرقان الذي يفرق بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Irāda has an original wāw, as related forms such as rāwadahu and rād; it means seeking the intended object and is its cause.
rows.anchor: والإرادة أصلها الواو لأنك تقول راودته على أن يفعل كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusr is the opposite of hardship and has related senses of wealth, the left hand, and a group sharing a camel in maysir; its root is ease.
rows.anchor: واليسر ضد العسر واليسار الغنى والسعة واليسار اليد اليسرى واليسر الجماعة يجتمعون على الجزور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of ʿusr is hardness; aʿsar can mean left-handed, and aʿsara can mean becoming poor, with ease as its opposite.
rows.anchor: وأصل العسر الصلابة يقال عسر الشيء عسرا ورجل أعسر يعمل بشماله وأعسر الرجل إذا افتقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbs كمل الشيء, أكمله, and كمّله all mean that something was completed or brought to completion.
rows.anchor: ويقال كمل الشيء وأكملته وكملته أي تممته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شهر رمضان may be nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, as apposition to الصيام, or as a subject whose relative clause or description supplies an omitted predicate.
rows.anchor: شهر رمضان في ارتفاعه ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramadan does not take nunation because it is definite and ends in the augmented alif and nūn resembling the feminine dual endings.
rows.anchor: لا ينصرف رمضان للتعريف وزيادة الألف والنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, شهر رمضان can also be accusative as the object of an implied command to fast, or in apposition to أياما.
rows.anchor: ويجوز في العربية شهر رمضان بالنصب من وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هدى is accusative as a circumstantial expression, meaning that the Qur'an guides people.
rows.anchor: في موضع النصب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here الشهر is an adverbial time expression meaning the person is resident in the town during Ramadan, not an object; otherwise a traveler who witnesses the month would also have to fast.
rows.anchor: فالشهر ينتصب على أنه ظرف لا على أنه مفعول به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attached pronoun in فليصمه is permissible through syntactic extension after الشهر has already been used adverbially.
rows.anchor: الاتساع وقع فيه بعد أن استعمل ظرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition in على سفر coordinates with the adjective مريضا because it has the sense of the noun مسافرا.
rows.anchor: وإنما عطف الظرف على الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same coordination of an adverbial phrase with an adjective appears in Yunus 10:12, where lying, sitting, and standing are coordinated forms.
rows.anchor: دعانا لجنبه أو قاعدا أو قائما

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats ولتكملوا as a coordinated sentence with an omitted clause, approximately: this was prescribed or intended so that you complete the count; he compares 6:75.
rows.anchor: عطف جملة على جملة لأن بعده محذوفا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj coordinates the phrase with the understood meaning of God's willing ease: He has made matters easy for you so that you complete the count.
rows.anchor: عطفا على تأويل محذوف ودل عليه ما تقدم من الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first grammatical analysis is illustrated by the wording in 6:75: God showed Abraham the kingdom so that he might become certain.
rows.anchor: إبراهيم ملكوت السماوات والأرض وليكون من الموقنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poem illustrates coordination with the inferred sense of an omitted part of the preceding statement; al-Zajjāj gives this analysis, while the first is al-Farrāʾ's.
rows.anchor: بادت وغير آيهن مع البلى إلا رواكد جمرهن هباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The counted days are identified as Ramadan, and it is singled out for fasting because of its special virtues: the Qur'an, on which religion and faith depend, was sent down in it.
rows.anchor: هذه الأيام المعدودات شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḥasan, and Qatāda say the whole Qur'an descended to the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr, then came to the Prophet piecemeal over twenty years; this is also transmitted from Abū ʿAbd Allāh.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير والحسن وقتادة وهو المروي عن أبي عبد الله

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says the Qur'an's revelation began on Laylat al-Qadr in Ramadan.
rows.anchor: ابتدأ إنزاله في ليلة القدر من شهر رمضان عن ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī, transmitting from Ibn ʿAbbās, says the year's needed revelation descended together to the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr, then was sent down in stages over months and days.
rows.anchor: في الشهور والأيام عن السدي بسنده إلى ابن عباس

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report through Abū Dharr attributes to the Prophet that Abraham's scriptures were sent down on the third of Ramadan.
rows.anchor:
أبي ذر الغفاري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:
" أنزلت صحف إبراهيم لثلاث مضين

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In the report's continuation, Abraham's scriptures are dated to the first or third night of Ramadan; Moses' Torah to the sixth, Jesus' Gospel to the thirteenth, David's Psalms to the eighteenth, and the Qur'an to the twenty-fourth. Al-ʿAyyāshī transmits this from al-Ṣādiq and his forefathers, ending with the Prophet.
rows.anchor: لأربع وعشرين من شهر رمضان وهذا بعينه رواه العياشي عن أبي عبد الله عن آبائه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes أنزل فيه القرآن to mean that the Qur'an was revealed concerning the obligation and prescription of fasting, with فيه meaning concerning its prescription.
rows.anchor: أنه أنزل في فرضه وإيجاب صومه على الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is guidance for people, directing them to the kinds of knowledge they are obligated to acquire, and its signs are proofs of guidance.
rows.anchor: دالا لهم على ما كلفوه من العلوم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the first guidance is guidance away from error, while the second means clarification of the lawful and unlawful.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالهدى الأول الهدى من الضلالة وبالثاني بيان الحلال والحرام عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Aṣamm and al-Qāḍī say the first guidance is the initial knowledge required of people; the second comprises accounts of prophets, their laws, and histories, which are known through the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وقيل أراد بأول ما كلف من العلم وبالثاني ما يشتمل عليه من الأنبياء وشرائعهم وأخبارهم لأنها لا تدرك إلا بالقرآن عن الأصم والقاضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Furqān is that which separates truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: أي ومما يفرق بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh distinguishes the Qur'an as the book as a whole from the Furqān, the decisive rulings that must be followed.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله ع أنه قال: القرآن جملة الكتاب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In a sermon reported by al-Bāqir through al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, Abū Ayyūb, and Abū al-Ward, the Prophet describes Ramadan's night better than a thousand months, obligatory fast, and voluntary night prayer worth seventy months' prayers; good deeds equal obligatory deeds elsewhere and an obligatory deed equals seventy. He calls it a month of patience, mutual aid, and increased provision; feeding a faster brings emancipation and forgiveness, even a sip of milk, water, or a few dates suffices, and easing a servant's work eases one's reckoning. He describes its beginning as mercy, middle as forgiveness, and end as answered prayer and release from fire; he urges testimony, asking for needs and Paradise, and seeking refuge from Hell.
rows.anchor: خطب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الناس في آخر جمعة من شعبان

rows.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
rows.claim: Salman al-Fārisī's version urges four practices: the testimony of faith and seeking forgiveness please God, while asking for Paradise and refuge from Hell are indispensable.
rows.anchor:
وفي رواية سلمان الفارسي
" فاستكثروا فيه من أربع خصال

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that a fasting person's sleep is worship, silence is glorification, prayer is answered, and deeds are multiplied.
rows.anchor:
وقال رسول الله:
" نوم الصائم عبادة وصمته تسبيح ودعاؤه مستجاب وعمله مضاعف "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stronger reading is that one who is present in town and not away during Ramadan must fast the whole month; الشهر is definite for the known month.
rows.anchor: فمن شهد منكم المصر وحضر ولم يغب في الشهر والألف واللام في الشهر للعهد والمراد به شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Asked about the wording, Abū Jaʿfar says it plainly means whoever witnesses Ramadan should fast it, while whoever travels in it should break the fast; this report is from Zurāra.
rows.anchor: ما رواه زرارة عن أبي جعفر أنه قال لما سئل عن هذه ما أبينها لمن عقلها قال من شهد رمضان فليصمه

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and other exegetes say that entering Ramadan while resident obliges fasting its entire month.
rows.anchor: وقد روي أيضا عن علي وابن عباس ومجاهد وجماعة من المفسرين أنهم قالوا: من شهد الشهر بأن دخل عليه الشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading takes the phrase to mean a legally responsible person who is resident when the month arrives must fast that month; it abrogates the earlier choice of fasting or fidya, since recitation order does not determine order of revelation. Tabrisi prefers the first reading.
rows.anchor: من شاهد منهم الشهر مقيما مكلفا فليصم الشهر بعينه وهذا نسخ للتخيير بين الصوم والفدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualifying illness is one that makes a person fear an extreme worsening of the illness.
rows.anchor: وحد المرض الذي يوجب الإفطار ما يخاف الإنسان معه الزيادة المفرطة في مرضه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abū Baṣīr reports that al-Ṣādiq leaves assessment of illness to the person: if weak, break the fast; if strong enough, fast, whatever the illness.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو بصير قال: سألت أبا عبد الله عن حد المرض الذي على صاحبه فيه الإفطار قال: هو مؤتمن عليه مفوض إليه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Another transmitted definition is any illness that prevents someone from standing for as long as a prayer; al-Ḥasan holds this, and jurists disagree.
rows.anchor: وروي أيضا: أن ذلك كل مرض لا يقدر معه على القيام بمقدار زمان صلاته وبه قال الحسن وفي ذلك اختلاف بين الفقهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Imāmī school, a journey allowing a fast to be broken is permitted or devotional and measures eight farsakhs, twenty-four miles; al-Shāfiʿī requires sixteen farsakhs and Abū Ḥanīfa twenty-four.
rows.anchor: وأما السفر الذي يوجب الإفطار عندنا فما كان مباحا أو طاعة وكانت المسافة ثمانية فراسخ أربعة وعشرين ميلا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and others require making up missed days immediately once the sick person recovers or the traveler returns.
rows.anchor: فقال الحسن وجماعة هي على التضييق إذا برىء المريض أو قدم المسافر

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa allows make-up days to be delayed; the Imāmī school sets the period before the next Ramadan, allows consecutive or separate days, and prefers consecutive days.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة موسع فيها وعندنا موقت بما بين رمضانين وتجوز متتابعة ومتفرقة والتتابع أفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If make-up fasting is delayed until another Ramadan arrives, fidya is due along with the make-up fast; al-Shāfiʿī agrees.
rows.anchor: فإن فرط حتى لحقه رمضان آخر لزمه الفدية والقضاء وبه قال الشافعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wills ease by granting the sick and traveler a dispensation not to fast during those circumstances.
rows.anchor: أي في الرخصة للمريض والمسافر إذ لم يوجب الصوم عليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes God's willing ease to apply to all human affairs.
rows.anchor: وقيل يريد الله بكم اليسر في جميع أموركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabrisi uses the verse against the compulsion doctrine: God wills ease in some human acts, does not will hardship in others, and therefore does not will imposing the impossible.
rows.anchor: وفيه دلالة على بطلان قول المجبرة لأنه بين أن في أفعال المكلفين ما يريده سبحانه وهو اليسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The completion is the make-up of the days missed through illness or travel, fasted after recovery or return; alternatively, the concession to break the fast was prescribed so the count could be completed later.
rows.anchor: أي تتموا عدة ما أفطرتم فيه وهي أيام السفر والمرض بالقضاء إذا أقمتم وبرأتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is completing the month's count: people without an excuse complete it then, while the sick and travelers complete it at another time.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون معناه ولتكملوا عدة الشهر لأنه مع الطاقة وعدم العذر يسهل عليه إكمال العدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who argue Ramadan is never shorter say the command requires an undiminished full count; Tabrisi answers that the required count may be twenty-nine or thirty days, or that the wording refers to making up missed days.
rows.anchor: أن المراد أكملوا العدة التي وجب عليكم صيامها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Imāmī school, this refers to the takbīr on the night of Eid al-Fiṭr after Maghrib, ʿIshāʾ, dawn, and the Eid prayer.
rows.anchor: المراد به تكبير ليلة الفطر عقيب أربع صلوات المغرب والعشاء الآخرة والغداة وصلاة العيد على مذهبنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others interpret it as saying the takbīr on Eid day.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وجماعة التكبير يوم الفطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is to magnify God for guiding people to the religious laws.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به ولتعظموا الله على ما أرشدكم له من شرائع الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's close means that people should thank God for His blessings.
rows.anchor: أي لتشكروا الله على نعمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaḍāʾ fundamentally means deciding a matter firmly; it can mean finishing rites, completing an act, decisively announcing something, or issuing a binding judgment.
rows.anchor: أصل القضاء فصل الأمر على إحكام وقد يفصل بالفراغ منه كقضاء المناسك وقد يفصل بأن يعمل على تمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalāq is an allotted share of good, originally a measure or entitlement; another derivation from khuluq makes it the share owed by noble character.
rows.anchor: والخلاق النصيب من الخير وأصله التقدير فهو النصيب من الخير على وجه الاستحقاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أشد is genitive in agreement with the comparison, though it is indeclinable here because its form matches a verb and it is an adjective; it can also be accusative as a verbal noun, with ذكرا as specification.
rows.anchor: أشد في موضع جلا ولكنه لا ينصرف لأنه على وزن الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: في الآخرة may attach to the phrase governed by the lām in له; من خلاق is a subject with له as its predicate, and من is extra. Alternatively, في الآخرة is an adverbial circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: في الآخرة الجار والمجرور يتعلق بما يتعلق به اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means after performing or finishing the rites. Mansak can mean a place of worship, so the phrase covers completing what is due there, or a verbal noun pluralized because rites contain many acts and utterances.
rows.anchor: المناسك: جمع المنسك والمنسك يجوز أن يكون موضع النسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes the commanded remembrance as the takbīr specific to the days of Minā, the recommended remembrance of those days.
rows.anchor: أن المراد به التكبير المختص بأيام منى لأنه الذكر المرغب فيه المندوب إليه في هذه الأيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view takes it as all supplications at those sacred stations, where prayer is better than elsewhere.
rows.anchor: أن المراد به سائر الأدعية في تلك المواطن لأن الدعاء فيها أفضل منه في غيرها

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir reports that pilgrims used to gather after the rites to recount their ancestors' boasts, deeds, and past exploits; God directed them to remember Him instead.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن أبي جعفر الباقر ع أنهم كانوا إذا فرغوا من الحج يجتمعون هناك ويعدون مفاخر آبائهم ومآثرهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda say to remember God's favors even more, since His blessings exceed those of ancestors and He bestowed their virtues as well as ours; this explains comparison of the obligatory remembrance with a lesser one.
rows.anchor: على ذلك بأن يذكروا نعم الله ويعدوا آلاءه

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ instead says to seek help and refuge in God as a child turns to and repeatedly calls for its father; Tabrisi prefers the preceding explanation.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه واستغيثوا بالله وافزعوا إليه كما يفزع الصبي إلى أبيه في جميع أموره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People at those sacred places fall into groups; one group asks only for worldly benefits and has no share of good in the afterlife because it does not believe in resurrection.
rows.anchor: بين سبحانه أن الناس في تلك المواطن أصناف فمنهم من يسأل نعيم الدنيا ولا يسأل نعيم الآخرة لأنه غير مؤمن بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this context, no khalāq means no substantial or abundant share of good in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: وما له في الآخرة من خلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kufans count two verses across 2:219–220 and treat تتفكرون as a verse ending; the other regional count has one verse and does not count that word as a verse ending.
rows.anchor: آيتان في الكوفي وآية واحدة فيما عد الكوفي تتفكرون آية وتركها غيره

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم
rows.claim: Kufan readers other than ʿĀṣim read إثم كثير with thāʾ, while the other readers use bāʾ and read إثم كبير.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم إثم كثير بالثاء والباقون بالباء

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr alone reads العفو in the nominative; the other readers use the accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحده قل العفو بالرفع والباقون بالنصب

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī supports كبير because كبير contrasts with صغير, while كبير denotes a grave sin; Qur'anic examples use صغير and كبير and call grave sins كبائر. The comparison أكبر also supports كبير rather than كثير.
rows.anchor: حجة من قرأ بالباء أن يقول الباء أولى لأن الكبر مثل العظم ومقابله الصغر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The كبير reading is supported by Qur'anic wording about every small and great matter being recorded and by references to major sins.
rows.anchor: وقد استعملوا في الذنب إذا كان موبقا الكبيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The كثير reading is supported by the following verse's account of Satan causing enmity and obstructing prayer and remembrance through wine and gambling, and a report that the Prophet cursed ten involved with wine.
rows.anchor: وجه قراءة من قرأ بالثاء أنه قد جاء فيهما إنما يريد الشيطان أن يوقع بينكم العداوة والبغضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument for كثير cites the Qur'anic description of Satan's effects through wine and gambling.
rows.anchor: إنما يريد الشيطان أن يوقع بينكم العداوة والبغضاء

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report curses ten wine-related parties: buyer and recipient, presser and commissioner, server and requester, carrier and recipient, and the consumer of its price.
rows.anchor: لعن الرسول في الخمر عشرة مشتريها والمشتراة له وعاصرها والمعصورة له وساقيها والمستقي لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For accusative العفو, ما ذا is one interrogative expression and ماذا ينفقون functions like ما ينفقون, asking what they spend; the answer is accusative.
rows.anchor: أن قولهم ماذا يستعمل على ضربين أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The single-expression analysis is illustrated by the idiom عما ذا تسأل and a poem asking ماذا بال نسوتكم, meaning ما بال نسوتكم.
rows.anchor: قول العرب عما ذا تسئل أثبتوا الألف في ما لما كان ما مع ذا بمنزلة اسم واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For nominative العفو, ذا means الذي, so the question means what is it that they spend; العفو answers as the predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: أن يجعل ماذا على الضرب الآخر فيكون تقديره ما الذي ينفقون فجوابه العفو على أن يكون خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about what God sent down is cited as a parallel for reading ذا as a relative pronoun.
rows.anchor: ماذا أنزل ربكم قالوا أساطير الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh allows ذا to mean الذي only in this construction; the Kufans permit it elsewhere and cite poetry and Moses' question, but Tabrisi rejects their evidence because the quoted phrases may be circumstantial expressions.
rows.anchor: سيبويه لا يجوز أن يكون ذا بمنزلة الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kufan evidence from Moses' question does not establish a relative-clause use, since بيمينك may be a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون ظرفا في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khamr derives from covering: foliage, a head covering, a concealing crowd, something mixed into a disease, and covering a vessel all illustrate the root.
rows.anchor: أصله الستر والخمر ما واراك

rows.speaker: كثير
rows.claim: The poet Kathīr uses مخامر for an affliction that mingles or remains mixed in, illustrating the root sense of khamr.
rows.anchor:
كثير:
هنيئا مريئا غير داء مخامر لعزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A small palm-fiber prayer mat is called khumra because it covers the face from the ground during prostration.
rows.anchor: كان النبي يسجد على الخمرة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj recounts that Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī realized an intoxicant sold under another name was wine's sibling; he cited a poem saying both were nursed by the same mother.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج وقد لبس على أبي الأسود الدؤلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maysir is gambling, named from yusr because the winner's share becomes due; the gambler is called yāsir because lots determine what is owed.
rows.anchor: من اليسر وهو وجوب الشيء لصاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another derivation links maysir to division: whatever is divided is yassartahu; yāsir and maysir can also name the camel being divided.
rows.anchor: وقيل أخذ من التجزئة لأن كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further derivation connects maysir to ease, since people joined to make sharing the camel easier, though they did so by gambling.
rows.anchor: وقيل أخذ من اليسر وهو السهولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿafw means increase or surplus, as in the description of a people increasing in number.
rows.anchor: العفو مأخوذ من الزيادة ومنه قيل حتى عفوا
